reason: The hypothesis synthesizes separate observations—high strain-rate deformation (P2, P16), intermediate-temperature ductility loss from grain boundary segregation (P12, P23, P26), and lattice friction from local chemical ordering (P1, P19)—into a new mechanistic chain where dynamic loading and thermal activation induce local chemical ordering that pins dislocations and causes brittle fracture. No single passage proposes this specific coupling of strain rate, temperature, and ordering to explain toughness loss, and the idea goes beyond the literature by linking these distinct phenomena through a mechanism none of the passages states.
